items.html: A fluent and strokeful middle order bat, Sanjay Raul got his first big break on the India 'A' tour of Pakistan in early 1998. An impressive unbeaten 115 in the third `Test' at Lahore was a pointer to his immense talent. In September, the Board, in typically ham-handed fashion, chose to split the Indian team between the Sahara Cup and the Commonwealth Games and Raul fortuitously slipped into the Toronto contingent. Batting at No's 7 and 8 in his two appearances, Raul failed either time. His placid off breaks were a trifle more successful, getting the better of Inzamam-ul-Haq on one occasion. His best domestic season was in 1996-97 when he topped the batting and bowling averages for Orissa with 644 runs and 37 wickets. (Sankhya Krishnan)
